The page must say 'effective [date]; we re-verify on/after that date' -- never 'is now in effect'. events.citation: D.C. Code Section 47-2853.49 (as amended by D.C. Act 26-399, Aug. 10, 2026, and made permanent by D.C. Law 26-183, Sept. 25, 2026)
events.summary_public: D.C.'s CPA practice-privilege (mobility) statute was amended by emergency legislation (D.C. Act 26-399, Business Licensing Reform and Accountancy Practice Emergency Amendment Act of 2026) effective August 10, 2026, replacing the prior NASBA substantial-equivalency verification requirement with a simpler test: a CPA whose principal place of business is not in D.C., who holds a valid, unrestricted out-of-state license in good standing, and who met exam/education/experience requirements at initial licensure now has automatic practice privileges in D.C. without an individual license. The same test became permanent law on September 25, 2026 (D.C. Law 26-183, Business Licensing Reform and Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2026). A savings clause preserves privileges already held under the prior version.

events.citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. (2026 Colo. Sess. Laws ch. 81 / SB26-076, signed 2026-05-04, eff. 2026-08-12)
events.summary_public: Colorado SB26-076 creates 3 new bachelor's-degree-based education/experience pathways to CPA certification (bachelor's + 2 yrs experience + ethics course + exam; bachelor's + 30 additional semester hours + 1 yr experience + ethics + exam; or post-baccalaureate degree + 1 yr experience + ethics + exam), available to applicants starting January 1, 2027. Separately, effective now (Aug 12, 2026), it grants practice-privilege mobility in Colorado, without the need to obtain a Colorado certificate, to an out-of-state CPA: an individual licensed or certified in good standing in another state or jurisdiction of the United States whose principal place of business is in that other state or jurisdiction, and who was required at initial licensure or certification there to pass the uniform CPA exam and hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university. The board may not require an out-of-state CPA to provide a notice, fee, or other submission as a condition of exercising these privileges, and privileges already held by out-of-state CPAs as of December 31, 2024 continue.
events.status_evidence: "The act expands the ways in which individuals may become eligible for certification as a certified public accountant (CPA) in Colorado by creating 3 new education and experience pathways"; "an individual CPA who is licensed or certified in good standing in another state or jurisdiction of the United States and whose principle place of business is located in another state or jurisdiction of the United States (out-of-state CPA) has all the same practice privileges as Colorado certificate holders, without the need to obtain a Colorado certificate"; "if the individual was required at their initial licensure or certification in the other state or jurisdiction of the United States to pass the uniform CPA examination and obtain a baccalaureate degree conferred by an accredited college or university"; "the board shall not require an out-of-state CPA to provide a notice, fee, or other submission" as a condition of exercising such practice privileges; "the act continues the practice privileges of out-of-state CPAs who held practice privileges in Colorado" as of December 31, 2024. (Note: this summary applies to this bill as enacted.) events.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. section 326.283
events.summary_public: A new enactment of the individual out-of-state CPA reciprocity/practice-privilege statute takes effect, replacing the version in effect since 2017. Under the new version, an individual whose principal place of business, domicile, or residency is not in Missouri and who holds a valid, unrestricted CPA license in good standing from any state may practice in Missouri without obtaining a Missouri license, notifying the board, or paying a fee, provided the individual met qualifying education/experience requirements at initial licensure (or held qualifying practice privileges as of 2024-12-31 under a grandfather provision).

events.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 326.289
events.summary_public: A 2026 amendment to Mo. Rev. Stat. § 326.289 adds a new exemption: a sole practitioner or single-member LLC using "certified public accountant(s)", "CPA", or a similar abbreviation in its business name may request exemption from the CPA firm-permit requirement by submitting a written request to the board affirming the business performs no attest services or other services subject to peer review. The amendment also updates peer-review equivalence/oversight-fee wording from "substantially equivalent" to "comparable".
events.status_evidence: New subdivision (5), effective 28 Aug 2026: "A sole practitioner or single member limited liability company (LLC) using the title of 'certified public accountant(s)', 'CPA', or similar abbreviation in their business name may request exemption from the firm permit requirements of paragraph (b) of subdivision (1) of this subsection by submitting a written request to the board that affirms the business does not offer nor perform attest services nor other services subject to peer review." (S.B. 1233, 103rd General Assembly; corroborated word-for-word by senate.mo.gov/26info/pdf-bill/perf/SB1233.pdf)

events.citation: Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04
events.summary_public: Alabama Board of Public Accountancy rule 30-X-3-.04 (practice privileges for nonresident certified public accountants) was amended, published August 31, 2026 and effective October 15, 2026. As amended, the practice privilege applies to a person who holds a valid active license in good standing as a CPA in another state, whose principal place of business is not in Alabama, and — if licensed after December 31, 2024 — who holds a minimum of a baccalaureate degree. The rule's published text does not show which words the amendment changed.

events.citation: Ala. Admin. Code 30-X-5-.02
events.summary_public: Alabama Board of Public Accountancy rule 30-X-5-.02 (CPE hours required) was amended, published August 31, 2026 and effective October 15, 2026. As amended, a licensee returning to active status applies for an annual permit to practice with forty CPE hours for each year not on active status, and one who has never elected active status and has been on inactive status more than five years applies with forty CPE hours for each year on inactive status (in either case not to exceed 120 hours); twenty percent of the hours must be in accounting and auditing courses and five percent in ethics courses, all obtained during the three-year period before the permit request. The rule's published text does not show which words the amendment changed.

events.citation: 59 O.S. Section 15.1 et seq. (as amended by HB4317, 2026); implementing rules proposed for OAC 10:15-3-2, 10:15-18-4, 10:15-21-1
events.summary_public: Oklahoma HB4317, effective November 1, 2026, adds a pathway to CPA licensure based on a bachelor's degree plus the CPA exam plus two years of supervised work experience, alongside the existing master's-degree and bachelor's-plus-30-credit-hour pathways. The Oklahoma Accountancy Board's Rule Impact Statement says HB4317 "simplifies the reciprocal application process" for CPAs licensed in states the Board has deemed substantially equivalent: instead of the five-option process that applies to all reciprocal applicants, such a CPA provides an interstate-exchange authorization or a letter of good standing, evidence of passing the AICPA ethics exam, and good-character evidence. The Board has two rule tracks. Its Rule Impact Statement (prepared August 21, 2026) is for emergency rules: because the permanent rulemaking process cannot be completed before HB4317's November 1, 2026 effective date, the Board says it is "promulgating these rules on an emergency basis", and that they "will remain in effect until superseded by permanent rules". Those emergency rules are conditional: the Board's September 2026 Bulletin says that on August 21, 2026 the Board "declared an emergency and approved the submission of these emergency rules to the Governor and the Legislature". The Bulletin said the Governor and Legislature "will have 45 days to approve or disapprove the rules" and that "If the rules are approved, they will become effective on November 1, 2026." That date has passed; the Board's rules page does not say whether the rules were approved and are in force. Its 2027 permanent rules (Proposed Permanent Rules Text, posted Oct 2026) are proposed, not yet final. Confirm rule status with the Board before relying on the new pathway.
events.status_evidence: Approved by Governor 2026-05-05 per the Oklahoma Legislature's own bill-status page for HB4317 (2026 session), with no later repeal, delay or amending action as of 2026-11-04; the Accountancy Board's official Rule Impact Statement (oklahoma.gov/oab) independently states HB4317 'takes effect November 1, 2026' and describes the statutory amendment in detail. The Board's published Sept 2026 rules compilation does not yet reflect HB4317; the Board's 2027 Proposed Permanent Rules Text (posted Oct 2026) would conform OAC 10:15-3-2, 10:15-18-4 and 10:15-21-1. Emergency track (SRC-264, re-read 2026-11-15): the Rule Impact Statement at secondary_url is titled "LICENSURE AND REGULATION OF ACCOUNTANCY EMERGENCY RULES", is dated "Prepared: August 21, 2026", and says "Because the standard permanent rulemaking process cannot be completed before that effective date, the Board is promulgating these rules on an emergency basis" and "These emergency rules will remain in effect until superseded by permanent rules adopted through the standard rulemaking process." The Board's rules page (citation_url, read 2026-11-15) has no mention of emergency rules or HB4317 and no longer links this RIS; the Board's September 2026 Bulletin (https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/oab/documents/bulletins/September%202026%20Bulletin.pdf, re-read 2026-11-15; Oct-Dec 2026 bulletins 404) says, in "HB4317 Implementation: Emergency Administrative Rules": "On Friday, August 21st, the Board declared an emergency and approved the submission of these emergency rules to the Governor and the Legislature. The Governor and Legislature will have 45 days to approve or disapprove the rules. If the rules are approved, they will become effective on November 1, 2026." (SRC-265); whether the emergency rules were approved and filed is not confirmed (resolve via the Secretary of State's emergency-rule filing record for OAC 10:15). Confirm rule status with the Board before relying on the new pathway. Rule Impact Statement (secondary_url): "HB4317 adds a new pathway to licensure based on a bachelor's degree plus the CPA exam plus two years of supervised work experience, alongside the Board's existing pathways (master's degree or bachelor's degree plus 30 credit hours, each paired with the CPA exam and one year of work experience)"; "HB4317 simplifies the reciprocal application process for CPAs licensed in states the Board has deemed substantially equivalent to Oklahoma. Rather than the five-option process that currently applies to all reciprocal applicants, a CPA from a substantially equivalent state need only provide" an interstate-exchange authorization or letter of good standing, AICPA ethics exam evidence, and good-character evidence.

events.summary_public: The Board of Accountancy's final regulation, effective November 4, 2026, eliminates the $20 fee for processing additional applications to take one or more sections of the CPA examination (the $120 initial-application fee stays). It also removes restrictions for re-examination requirements and clarifies CPA license eligibility requirements, clarifies statutes related to CPA firm ownership requirements, requires each Virginia license holder to notify the Board in writing within 30 calendar days of any significant change of control, ownership, or practice of regulated activities of a Virginia CPA firm, and repeals 18VAC5-22-30 as redundant. The Virginia Register also lists amendments to 18VAC5-22-50 (whether a person's or firm's principal place of business is in Virginia) and 18VAC5-22-150 (monitoring program and peer review), but the codified Virginia Administrative Code does not yet show either section as amended. We are re-checking those two against the codified text before treating them as settled.

events.citation: A.R.S. § 32-725, as amended by Laws 2026, Ch. 17 (SB 1181, Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026), eff. 2027-01-01
events.summary_public: A.R.S. § 32-725 (Arizona's limited reciprocity privilege statute) covers both individuals and business organizations, not individuals alone. For individuals, the statute will replace its current qualification path — which relies on the individual's other jurisdiction itself requiring 150 semester hours of education, a passing CPA exam, and a year of experience, or direct qualification under 32-721(C) — with a new path, effective January 1, 2027: meeting Arizona's own 32-721(A)/32-4302 standards, or holding a valid active CPA license from any jurisdiction as of December 31, 2024. Through December 31, 2026, the 150-hour/exam/experience test remains the in-force law. That is only one of four cumulative requirements: the individual's principal place of business must be outside Arizona, they must not have or represent having an Arizona office, and they must not be under license suspension, revocation, or relinquishment.
events.status_evidence: Enacted text, NOT YET IN FORCE (effective 2027-01-01 per Laws 2026, Ch. 17 (SB 1181), Sec. 18: "This act is effective from and after December 31, 2026" -- confirmed directly against the enacted act text, not just the bill-status page): "(a) The individual meets the qualifications prescribed in either: (i) Section 32-721, subsection A. (ii) Section 32-4302. (b) The individual holds a valid active registration, certificate or license as a certified public accountant from any jurisdiction as of December 31, 2024." IN-FORCE text through 2026-12-31 (same statute, prior to the 2027-01-01 effective date): "(a) The other jurisdiction requires as a condition of licensure that an individual has all of the following: (i) At least one hundred fifty semester hours of college education... (ii) A passing grade on the uniform certified public accountant examination. (iii) At least one year of experience in the practice of accounting that has been verified. (b) The individual meets the qualifications prescribed in section 32-721, subsection C." Subsection B's full cumulative list (verified against current page 2026-10-14): "B. To qualify to exercise the limited reciprocity privilege, an individual must: 1. Have a principal place of business that is not in this state. 2. Not have or represent to have an office in this state. 3. Not be the subject of suspension or revocation of a certificate... 4. Hold a valid registration, certificate or license... and either of the following applies: [B.4(a)/(b) above]". azleg.gov's live page (re-fetched this pass, 200, 6,004 bytes) shows ONLY the post-2027 (a)/(b) text (0 hits for "150 semester", "semester hours", "one year", "32-721, subsection C"; 1 hit for "32-4302") with no amendment/effective-date marker (0 hits for "amended", "Laws 20", "effective date", "session law", "repeal") -- the page cannot be relied on to tell current vs. future law apart; the effective date comes from the act text, not the statute page.

events.summary_public: Louisiana Act 653 (HB548) amends Louisiana's CPA licensure and mobility law, effective August 1, 2026. Key changes: new 3-pathway education requirement, repeal of the "substantial equivalency" standard in favor of a "mobility"/"comparable" standard for practice privileges and foreign-designation reciprocity, a grandfather clause for CPAs already holding LA practice privileges as of Dec 31, 2024, and a board-composition diversity requirement. This is the CPA-Evolution/mobility-model reform pattern also seen in Colorado, Missouri, Idaho, and Oklahoma this year.
events.status_evidence: Bill-status action history (BillInfo.aspx?s=26rs&b=HB548): 'Effective date: 08/01/2026.' Louisiana Board of CPAs public pamphlet: signed June 2, 2026, effective August 1, 2026. The enrolled Act text (Sections 1-2) carries no effective-date clause of its own -- 'Effective January 1, 2027' appears only in the non-authoritative Resume Digest summary (d=1486852) and is not corroborated by any primary source.

events.citation: IDAPA 24.30.01, Docket No. 24-3001-2601: Notice of Rulemaking, Adoption of Pending Rule, Idaho Administrative Bulletin, Nov 4 2026, Vol 26-11, pp. 35-40 (proposed rule: Aug 5 2026, Vol 26-8, pp. 31-33); pending-rule approval by concurrent resolution and effective date: Idaho Code § 67-5224(2)(c), as named in the bulletin's own effective-date statement
events.summary_public: Idaho's Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses adopted Docket No. 24-3001-2601 (IDAPA 24.30.01) as a pending rule, published in the Nov 4, 2026 Idaho Administrative Bulletin, Vol. 26-11. It is not final: it goes into effect only if the 2027 Idaho Legislature approves it by concurrent resolution, and if approved it becomes final and effective July 1 of the year of that session, unless the resolution states a different date. The Division's August 2026 notice says the rulemaking "facilitates a new pathway to licensure for candidates and makes minor adjustments to accommodate for statutory changes in line with HB 563 from 2026" and "removes outdated language." The adoption notice lists two changes from the proposed text: matching AICPA language in Paragraph 107.02.d, and shifting licensure periods from annual to biennial terms. The pending text provides that, beginning January 1, 2028, licenses expire at midnight on the licensee's legal birthday during the second year of a two-year term instead of every June 30 (Rule 108.01); a late renewal is one made no more than 30 days after expiration, replacing the July 1 to August 1 window (Rule 108.03); firms file a registration biennially instead of annually, still no later than September 30 (Rule 211.01); and biennial fee amounts are added, including $240 for an active license (Rule 400). The current rules stay in force unless and until it is approved.
events.status_evidence: NOTICE OF RULEMAKING - ADOPTION OF PENDING RULE ... This rule has been adopted by the agency and is now pending review by the 2027 Idaho State Legislature and must be approved by concurrent resolution of the Legislature to go into effect ... Should the pending rule be approved, it will become final and effective on July 1 following the First Regular Session of the Sixty-ninth Legislature, unless the concurrent resolution states a different effective date. ... Two changes have been made to this rule's text, to: (1) Match professional language in Paragraph 107.02.d. set out by the Association of International Certified Public Accountants; and (2) shift licensure periods from annual to biennial terms to align with the Division's operational shift to biennial birthdate renewal. August 5, 2026 Bulletin, Vol. 26-8 (secondary_url), Docket No. 24-3001-2601 descriptive summary: "This contemplated rulemaking: (1) facilitates a new pathway to licensure for candidates and makes minor adjustments to accommodate for statutory changes in line with HB 563 from 2026; (2) transitions from June 30 to birthdate-based renewals with an expanded window to accommodate peak tax season; and (3) removes outdated language."

events.citation: 22 GCA § 35122 (Substantial Equivalency), Guam Accountancy Act of 2003; firm permits at 22 GCA § 35107; implementing rules at 25 GAR §§ 2103(d), 2106, 2112
events.secondary_citation: 25 GAR Ch. 2, Guam Accountancy Administrative Rules (incl. the § 2103(d)(2)(B)(iv) $175 fee)
events.summary_public: Guam's own primary legal sources don't agree with each other on this rule. Rather than guess, we found the conflict and are showing you exactly where it is below — read both citations yourself, or confirm directly with the Guam board.
events.conflict_summary: Guam's codified statute (22 GCA § 35122(a)) grants the practice privilege automatically — no notice, no other submission, and no license are required — and the statute is silent on fees. But the Board's own rules, which the statute conditions the privilege on complying with (§ 35122(a)(3)(B)), impose an ongoing $175 annual renewal fee for the same privilege (25 GAR § 2103(d)(2)(B)(iv)), with no fee authorized anywhere in § 35122 itself. The statute and the rule were both touched by the same act, P.L. 33-193 (2016).

events.summary_public: Oregon's own primary legal sources don't agree with each other on this rule. Rather than guess, we found the conflict and are showing you exactly where it is below — read both citations yourself, or confirm directly with the Oregon board.
events.conflict_summary: Oregon's compiled rule (OAR 801-010-0345(3)) requires out-of-state firm registration for a broader set of attest engagements (including SSARS reviews) than the statute (ORS 673.160) actually triggers, and the Board's own peer-review guidance page follows the narrower statutory reading rather than its own compiled rule.

events.citation: Act 140 of 1947, as amended by P.L.563, No.57 (amended Oct. 8, 2026)
events.summary_public: Section 4.2 of Act 140 of 1947 sets the requirements for issuance of a CPA certificate; its subsection (b)(3) sets the education required. Clause (ii) of (b)(3) was amended Oct. 8, 2026 (P.L.563, No.57). As amended, clause (ii) requires a baccalaureate degree and at least twenty-four semester credits in accounting and auditing, business law, economics, technology, finance or tax subjects, plus an additional twelve semester credits in accounting and auditing subjects or tax subjects, of a content satisfactory to the board. Clause (iii) (a master's or other post-graduate degree) was amended by the same act and, as amended, carries the same additional-twelve-credit requirement. The additional credits need not be part of undergraduate or graduate work. Under subsection (f), after passing the examination a candidate meeting clause (i) or (iii) may be issued a certificate with at least one year of qualifying experience, or one meeting clause (ii) with at least two years. Eligibility to take the examination is set separately: subsection (b.1) (amended June 30, 2025, P.L.85, No.27) lets an individual take it with a baccalaureate degree or at least one hundred twenty semester credits of post-secondary education, plus the age and good-moral-character requirements of (b)(1) and (2). Act 57 took effect immediately on approval, Oct. 8, 2026. The statute's amendment notes do not show the prior text.
